blocks.value: Every program you have written so far knows its own answers in advance. The values are baked into the source, so it prints the same thing every run.
A program becomes useful the moment someone else can put their values into it. This lesson is that step, and it is the one where your programs start to feel real.
What you will be able to do
By the end of this lesson you will be able to:

items: Read values from the keyboard with the `Scanner` class
Choose the right `Scanner` method for each data type
Control the format of output with `printf` and format specifiers
